Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 2:

(p-104) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah As-Saff

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (2) ﴿Great hatred in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do.﴾ (3) ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly.﴾ (4).

In the first verse there is a rebuke against those who say what they do not do. In the second verse there is an explanation of the intensity of Allah's anger and hatred toward those who are like that. But it is not stated here what the saying contrary to the action is, which is forbidden and for which they are reproached and which deserves intense anger. However, the coming of the third verse after them indicates the subject of saying and doing, which is jihad in the cause of Allah.

The scholars of tafsir (tafsir: exegesis of the Qur'an) agree that the occasion of revelation, although it is multiple in their view, concerns jihad in the cause of Allah, from a desire to be permitted to take part in jihad and to know the most beloved of deeds to Allah, and the like.

The Qur'an has explained in several places that the subject of the first and second verses concerns jihad and their wishing for it. Among that is His saying, may He be exalted, concerning them: ﴿And those who believed say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?" But when a decisive surah was sent down and fighting was mentioned therein, you saw those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death.﴾ [Muhammad: 20].

And among them is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not considered those who were told, "Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear men as they should fear Allah or with greater fear and say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us to a near term."﴾ [An-Nisa: 77].

And among them is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs; and the covenant of Allah is ever questioned.﴾ (p-105) [Al-Ahzab: 15].

In the first verse: they wished for the sending down of a surah in which permission for fighting is given, and when it was sent down, those sick at heart became like one fainting from death.

In the second: they were told, "Restrain your hands from fighting," so they wished for permission for it, and when it was prescribed for them, they turned back and wished, "If only they were postponed to a near term."

In the third: they had given covenants to be steadfast and not to turn back, and the covenant of Allah is ever questioned. Then when it came to Uhud, what happened happened, and likewise at Hunayn. What also bears witness to this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return." And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed," and they were not exposed. They intended only to flee.﴾ ﴿And if they had been entered from its surrounding areas and then they had been asked to commit sedition, they would have given it, and they would not have hesitated therein except briefly.﴾ ﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs.﴾ The verse [Al-Ahzab: 13-15].

In this context there is an explanation of their reproach for breaking the covenant, and this is the meaning of "why do you say what you do not do," exactly the same. In contrast to this, Allah, may He be exalted, praised another group of them when they fulfilled the covenant and were truthful in what they had covenanted with Allah, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah. Among them is he who has fulfilled his obligation [by death], and among them is he who awaits, and they have not altered [their pledge] in the least.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 23].

Then He explained the difference between the two groups in His saying after it: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills or accept their repentance. Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage; they gained no good.﴾ The verses [Al-Ahzab: 24-25], and that was at the Battle of the Confederates.

Thus it becomes clear from this that the action contrary to the saying here is not fulfilling the covenant which they had bound upon themselves beforehand, so they deserved reproach for it. It is also clear that those who fulfilled the covenant deserved praise for fulfilling it. The verse has been cited, by the generality of its wording, as a condemnation of everyone whose action contradicts his saying, whether in a covenant, a promise, a command, or a prohibition.

As for commands and prohibitions, like His saying: ﴿Do you order the people to piety and forget yourselves?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 44].

And like His saying about the Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb to his people: ﴿And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from.﴾ [Hud: 88].

(p-106) As for covenant, His saying: ﴿And fulfill the covenant; indeed, the covenant is ever questioned.﴾ [Al-Isra: 34].

From this angle, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him, examined it in several places, among them in Surah Hud at the saying of Shu'ayb mentioned above.

And among them at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾ [Maryam: 54], in Surah "Maryam".

He examined therein the fulfillment of promise, the difference between promise and threat, and fulfillment of promise and breaking of threat, and he set up an issue for it, and cited the two verses of "As-Saff" there.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly together﴾ [al-Saff: 4].

The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) differed over the meaning of "a structure joined firmly together" (al-bunyan al-marsus). Some of them transmitted from al-Farra' that it refers to a structure bonded with lead (al-rasas) because of its great strength, while the majority hold that it refers to a structure whose parts are tightly adjacent, compact and even.

The reality is that the intended point of comparison here is the aspect of resemblance, and it cannot be that the comparison is to the form of the building alone, nor to its being bonded with lead, nor to its being inseparable, nor to its evenness and compactness; for that would conflict with the nature of advancing and withdrawing on the battlefield, and every encounter has its own arrangement according to its position.

What appears, and Allah knows best, is that the intended aspect of resemblance here is the general quality of strength and unity.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that he means the evenness of their stance in steadfastness, so that they are, in unity of word, like a structure joined firmly together. End of quotation.

The following supports this:

First, the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when you left your family in the morning to settle the believers in positions for battle; and Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 121].

Here "positions" (maqa'id) refers to the places assigned to the groups of the army, which is the deployment (al-ta'biah) according to the circumstances of the engagement, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) did in placing the archers at the Battle of Uhud to protect their rear from the enemy's encircling them due to the nature of the place, and as he did at the Battle of Badr, when he aligned them and made them even with a staff in his hand, also due to the nature of the place.

Thus, in every engagement there must be consideration of its position, and indeed of the conditions of the weapons and the fighters.

The author of al-Jumman in the Similitudes of the Qur'an mentioned the parts and divisions of the army in general terms: the center, the right wing, the left wing, the flanks, and the like. So the aspect of resemblance is the moral bond, the sense of responsibility, and the awareness of duty, as Al-Habbab ibn al-Mundhir did at the Battle of Badr when he looked at the position of the Muslims from the site and did not approve of it; he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), received his answer, then put forward a new plan, which he (ﷺ) adopted, and he changed the position from its place in the battlefield.

Second, the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful. And obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ [al-Anfal: 45-46].

Here He mentioned, among the factors of victory: steadfastness at the encounter, the remembrance of Allah and obedience, compliance, preserving these by avoiding dispute, and patience at the charge and the struggle, so that it becomes as the charge of one man. All of these fall under the meaning of "a structure joined firmly together" in its strength, its protection and its steadfastness. Allah has also censured the Jews for the scattering of their hearts in battle, in His saying: ﴿You think them united, but their hearts are divided﴾ [al-Hashr: 14], and He praised the believers for their unity in fighting, as if they were a structure joined firmly together.

The Sunnah has also come with this comparison for cooperation, in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it strengthening another.»

This clarifies the intended aspect of resemblance in "a structure joined firmly together" here. It is also related from Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said to his companions: "Adhere to obedience, for it is the fortress of the warrior."

And from Aktham ibn Sayfi: "Minimize disagreement with your commanders."

Today the Muslims are in the greatest need of adhering to this noble Qur'anic guidance in facing their common cause with their shared enemy, especially since the Islamic world has passed through several experiences in its long history, from which it has drawn the clearest lessons. In this Qur'anic method they have the strongest reason to recover their rights and preserve their existence, in addition to its being the work that Allah loves from His servants. And success is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 5:

(p-108) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you cause me harm while you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?" So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

The statement of Moses, peace be upon him: "Why do you cause me harm?" He did not specify the kind of this harm. A similar generality occurs in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69]

Ibn Kathir referred to it in his tafsir and cited the hadith of al-Bukhari that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Moses, peace be upon him, was modest and very private; no part of his skin was seen out of modesty. So those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He conceals himself in this manner only because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a swelling of the testicles, or some affliction.' Allah, mighty and majestic, wished to clear him of what they said. So one day he was alone, he took off his clothes onto a rock, then bathed. When he finished, he turned to his clothes to take them, but the rock ran off with his garment. Moses took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he reached a group of the Children of Israel, who saw him naked, in the best form that Allah, mighty and majestic, had created, and Allah cleared him of what they said." ... to the end of the story.

Other exegetes also transmitted it at this point. According to this, their harm to him was personal harm, by claiming a defect in him in his creation. Although this is valid for the verse of al-Ahzab, because of His saying: ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69], it is not valid for this verse of "al-Saff", because his saying to them: ﴿while you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you﴾ [al-Saff: 5] indicates that the harm was in regard to the message, not his personal side. It is supported by His saying immediately after it: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5].

That is: when they deviated by what they harmed him with, so their harming of their people to him here is harm of deviation and misguidance. They harmed him greatly in this, as Allah explained in His saying about them: ﴿And when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55].

Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We took your covenant and raised above you the mount, "Take what We have given you with determination and listen." They said, "We hear and disobey." And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf because of their disbelief. Say, "Evil is that which your faith orders you to do, if you are believers."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 93].

Behold, the covenant is taken from them and the mount is raised above them, and it is said to them: ﴿Take what We have given you with determination and listen.﴾ (p-109) All of this is equivalent to His saying: ﴿And you certainly know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you﴾, because "qad" here is for emphasis (tahqiq). Yet they harm him by their saying: ﴿We hear and disobey﴾, and they harm him by being made to drink into their hearts the love of the calf and its worship because of their disbelief. Therefore he said to them: ﴿Evil is that which your faith orders you to do, if you are believers.﴾

The harming of the disbelievers of the Messenger of Allah has been combined with the harming of Moses's people of Moses in His saying: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. They had asked Moses for greater than that, when they said, "Show us Allah outright," so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Nisa': 153], and so on.

From the totality of this it becomes clear that the harm stated here is specifically regarding the message. There is no barrier to their having harmed him with kinds of harm to his person, and in what he brought, ﴿so Allah cleared him of what they said﴾ in the verse of "al-Ahzab", and [Allah] punished them for their harming him in what he was sent with to them by the deviation of their hearts. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, the shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) previously discussed this meaning in surah "al-Rum", in discussing His saying: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst, because they denied the signs of Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 10] and so on.

He said: Disbelief and denial may, through their ill omen, lead to the wretchedness of their possessor, and he cited this verse: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾

And His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10].

He referred, for the verse of "Bani Isra'il", to His saying: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-An'am: 25].

And for the surah of "al-A'raf", to His saying: ﴿So they were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers﴾ [al-A'raf: 101].

Among what bears witness to this general meaning by the converse analogy is His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness﴾ [Muhammad: 17], and its like.

Among what draws attention here is the ascription of deviation to the hearts in His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾.

(p-110) And guidance is also to the heart, as in His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Taghabun: 11].

For this reason the believers were eager for this supplication: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾ [Al 'Imran: 8], which includes both meanings. And Allah knows best.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-415) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Saff

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

This noble verse indicates by its apparent meaning that one who departs from obedience to Allah is not guided by Allah.

Other verses have come indicating the opposite, such as His saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease...﴾ [al-Anfal: 38], and not all of it.

And His saying: ﴿Thus were you before, then Allah bestowed favor upon you﴾ [al-Nisa': 94].

The answer is that the verse is of the general that is specified (al-'amm al-makhsus); it refers specifically to the wretched whom Allah caused their hearts to deviate from guidance because of their eternal wretchedness.

It has been said: the meaning is that He does not guide them as long as they remain in their defiance; if they repent from it, He guides them.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 61, verse 6:

﴿And when Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what was before me of the Torah and giving good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad."﴾

Musa is mentioned without the good tidings of the Prophet (ﷺ) being mentioned with him, while Isa is mentioned and the good tidings are mentioned with him. By its implied meaning (mafhum, the implicature of a proper name, mafhum al-laqab), this suggests that only Isa (peace be upon him) gave the good tidings of him. However, the wording "Isa" is an implicature of a proper name (mafhum al-laqab), and the jurists of legal theory (al-Usuliyyun, the scholars of usul al-fiqh) do not act upon it. All the prophets gave the good tidings of him (ﷺ), and among them is Musa (peace be upon him). What points to Musa giving the good tidings of him is the statement of Isa (peace be upon him) in this verse: ﴿confirming what was before me﴾, and what was before him is the Torah, which was revealed to Musa.

The description of him (ﷺ) and of those with him has also come explicitly in the Torah, in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is the messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

Likewise, their description has come in the Gospel in the same context, in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot, then strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands upon its stalk﴾ [al-Fath: 29], to the end of the surah.

The text concerning all the prophets has also come, in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My burden upon that?" They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 81].

Ibn Kathir said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah did not send any prophet without taking from him the covenant that: "If he is sent while you are alive, you will surely follow him," and He took from him that he should take the same covenant from his nation: "If Muhammad is sent while they are alive, they will surely follow him and support him." End of quote.

The confirmation of this came in the story of the Negus (al-Najashi) when he heard from Ja'far (concerning the Prophet (ﷺ)): "I bear witness that he is the messenger of Allah, and that he is the one we find in the Gospel, and that he is the one whom Isa the son of Maryam gave good tidings of." And what he also said: (p-111) "By Allah, were it not for the kingship that I am in, I would have gone to him, until I would carry his sandals and perform ablution for him," in a long hadith which Ibn Kathir related and attributed to Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him.

Likewise was the supplication of the prophet of Allah, Ibrahim (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet): ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 129].

For this reason he (ﷺ) said: "I am the answer to the supplication of my father Ibrahim, and the good tidings of Isa, and the dream of my mother, which she saw."

Isa was singled out for explicit mention of the good tidings of him (ﷺ), because he is the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, so he conveys those good tidings to his people from what came before him.

As He said: ﴿confirming what was before me of the Torah﴾, and whoever came before him conveys from whoever came before him, and so on, until Isa (peace be upon him) explicitly stated it and delivered it to his people.

As for His saying: ﴿whose name is Ahmad﴾, the text has come that he (ﷺ) has a number of names. In the Sahih is his saying (ﷺ): "I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser) by whom Allah erases disbelief, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-'Aqib (the Last)."

On this occasion he (ﷺ) is mentioned by his name Ahmad here, and by his name Muhammad in the surah "Muhammad" (ﷺ).

He (ﷺ) is also mentioned with many attributes, the most comprehensive of which is what is considered an autobiography from Allah the Exalted about His messenger (ﷺ), in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128].

More explanation of this will come, God willing, at the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed you are of great moral character﴾ [al-Qalam: 4].

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, had already explained this at His saying: ﴿Their argument is futile in the sight of their Lord﴾ [al-Shura: 16] in Surat al-Shura, and at His saying: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 18] in Surat al-Anbiya.

[p-112] The trade is explained by His words, exalted is He: ﴿You believe in God and His Messenger, and strive in the way of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Saff: 11].

Trade (tijarah) is the disposal of capital in pursuit of profit, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿except that it be a present trade that you conduct among yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282], and He said: ﴿and a trade whose slump you fear﴾ [al-Tawbah: 24].

Here the trade has been explained as belief in God and His Messenger, and the expending of wealth and self in the way of God. What is the exchange in that important trade? God has clarified it in His words: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for their having Paradise. They fight in the way of God, so they kill and are killed. It is a promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in the transaction you have concluded. That is the great triumph﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111]. Here there is a transaction, here there is good news, and here there is a great triumph.

Likewise in this verse: ﴿He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great triumph﴾, ﴿and another [favour] you love: victory from God and an imminent conquest﴾ [al-Saff: 12–13].

The Qur'an has indicated that whoever misses this profitable bargain is certainly a loser, as in His words: ﴿They are the ones who purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their commerce has not profited them, nor were they guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16].

The reality of this trade is that the capital of a person is his life, and its end is his death.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every person goes out in the morning selling himself, either freeing himself or destroying himself." The Arabs knew this sale in the sense of exchange, as the poet said:

"Though you claim I was ignorant among you, I have bought forbearance after you with ignorance."

And another said:

"I exchanged the full locks for a bald head, and the bright front teeth for the gap-toothed ones, just as the Muslim buys [Christianity] when he becomes a Christian."

So he applied the word "buying" to exchange.

Note

[p-113] In this noble verse, striving with wealth is mentioned before striving with the self, in His words: ﴿and strive in the way of God with your wealth and your lives﴾.

In the verse ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers﴾, He placed the self before wealth, saying: ﴿purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾, and in that there is a subtle secret.

As for the verse of al-Saff, the context is one of explanation and clarification of the meaning of the profitable trade through striving (jihad, exertion) in the way of God.

The reality of jihad is the expenditure of effort and capacity. Wealth is the sinew of war and the supply of the army. It is more important than fighting with weapons, for weapons are bought with wealth. Men may also be hired, as in modern armies from foreign units, and the army is equipped with wealth. Therefore, when the command to fight came, God excused the sick and the weak, and excused with them the poor who cannot equip themselves, and excused with them the Messenger (ﷺ) when nothing was found with him to equip them, as in His words: ﴿No blame is upon the weak or the sick﴾, up to His words: ﴿nor upon those who came to you that you might mount them, and you said, "I can find nothing to mount you on." They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears from grief that they could not find anything to spend﴾ [al-Tawbah: 91–92].

Likewise, from another aspect, one may strive with wealth who cannot strive with weapons, such as women and the weak, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever equips a fighter has himself fought."

As for the second verse, it is in the context of exchange, offer and demand, or what is called bargaining. He placed the self first, because it is the dearest thing a living person possesses, and set against it Paradise, which is the dearest thing to be granted. The best that has been said on this is:

"I bargain with the precious self, whose Lord, and for whom among all creation there is no price. By it the other [life] is obtained, so if I sell it for something of this world, that is the loss. If my self is lost for a worldly thing I obtain, then my self is lost, and the price is lost too."

So the trade here is a dealing with God through faith in God and His Messenger, and striving with wealth and self, and the righteous deed in that, as was also said:

"I bargain with the precious self, whose Lord, and for whom among all creation there is no price."

[p-114] And another said:

"Work for your self before death, striving diligently, for profit and loss lie only in deeds."

In the verse ﴿Indeed, God has purchased﴾ there is a subtle, hidden good news of victory for those who strive in the way of God. It lies in the placement of His words: "so they kill" (fa-yaqtulūna) in the active voice, meaning "so they kill their enemy," and "and are killed" (wa-yuqtalūna) [al-Tawbah: 111] in the passive voice. The placement here suggests that they kill the enemy before he kills them, and they strike him before he strikes them. Such a case belongs to a position of strength and victory, and God knows best.

**Verse 14 of Surah al-Saff** (the commentary's opening): "﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah, as Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples [al-ḥawāriyyūn], 'Who are my helpers for Allah?'…﴾" and so on.

In this verse there is also an indication to the Muslims of victory, in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So We strengthened those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾ [al-Saff: 14]. However, it does not make clear whether they were the helpers of Allah in the way the disciples were the helpers of Allah, or not.

Indeed, there is something that indicates that they were actually the helpers of Allah, as was mentioned earlier in Surah al-Hashr, in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿[It is] for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and approval and helping Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful﴾ [al-Hashr: 8].

Likewise the Ansar (the Helpers of Medina), in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the foremost [in precedence] of the first emigrants and the helpers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100]. And as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. So "forceful against the disbelievers" is the meaning of "helping Allah and His Messenger."

Then came the parable given about them of mutual support and cooperation, in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. So He named them helpers, and He made clear their support, whether they were from the emigrants or the Helpers. May Allah's approval be upon them all. And Allah knows best.
